source.title_on_document: Creative or Uncreative Partner: Comparing Humans and AI in Collaborative Creative Tasks

supplement.where: Referred to as 'supplementary information' (SI 1, SI 2); no URL given in the document. Preregistration at https://osf.io/tveaf.
supplement.holds: SI 1: protocol for deriving a DAT score for ChatGPT-4o (p. 5). SI 2: further analysis details for the short story diversity analysis (p. 7). Deviations and exploratory analyses not on the registry (p. 4). Main-text tables already give coefficients and SEs for AUT models.

paper_design_summary: 208 Prolific participants were randomly assigned to collaborate in turn-taking chat either with another participant (human-human, 68 pairs) or with a prompted GPT-4o partner (human-AI, 72 pairs); within each pair, roles A (goes first) and B were also randomly assigned. Pairs completed two Alternate Uses Task trials (bottle, book) and a 10-minute one-sentence-per-turn short story. AUT originality was scored with CLAUS, story originality with divergent semantic integration (DSI), and diversity with forward flow, Levene's test on originality scores, and a Sentence-BERT diversity contribution score across stories; word count measured elaboration.

studies.label: Collaborative AUT and short story writing with a human vs GPT-4o partner (Prolific)

assignment.what_was_assigned: Partner type: human partner (human-human pair) vs GPT-4o partner (human-AI pair). Separately, role A (initiates turns) vs role B.
assignment.quote: Upon taking part in the study, participants were randomly assigned to either a human-AI (72 pairs) or human-human (68 pairs) condition.
assignment.prereg_locator: p. 3, Methods: 'pre-registered on the Open Science Framework (OSF) ... https://osf.io/tveaf'

arms.name: Human-AI
arms.description: Participant takes turns with ChatGPT-4o (prompt-engineered as a creative collaborator) in a chat interface matched to the human condition; 5-second (AUT) or 10-second (story) response delay.

arms.name: Human-human
arms.description: Participant takes turns with another Prolific participant, matched via SMARTRIQS.

participants.exclusions: Data were removed for participants who admitted using external internet or AI resources (p. 6); the number removed is not stated, and it is not stated whether 208 is before or after removal. Table 1 reports n = 208 (AI 72, Human 136). AUT mixed models use 139 groups (137 in the human-only model), so one pair is missing from the AUT analysis without explanation (pp. 9-10, Table 2; p. 13, Table 3). Story diversity test uses 72 vs 68 pairs (p. 15).
participants.who: Prolific participants; mean age 35.18 (SD 12.07); 54.8 percent female; 97.1 percent English first language; paid $6 for 30 minutes.
participants.quote: A total of 208 participants were recruited from Prolific for the study.

ai_tool.name_model: ChatGPT-4o (GPT-4o) via OpenAI API, hosted through PythonAnywhere
ai_tool.how_used: AI acts as a turn-taking co-creator: it alternates with the participant, contributing its own AUT ideas or story sentences (as role A or role B). Prompted to generate original ideas. Outputs scored include the AI's contributions unless the 'human-only' models exclude them.

task.description: Two collaborative AUT trials (bottle, book; 3 minutes each, alternating ideas) and a collaborative creative short story from the words 'stamp-letter-send' (one sentence per turn, 10 minutes). Story task would be creative_writing. Afterwards each participant individually completed the Divergent Association Task (DAT).
task.duration: about 30 minutes in total; AUT 3 minutes per object; story 10 minutes

outcomes.name: AUT originality, all responses in the pair (human and AI)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Originality of each AUT response scored by CLAUS (Cross-Lingual Alternate Uses Scoring, a transformer fine-tuned to human ratings, hosted on the Creativity Assessment Platform). Mixed model: originality ~ condition * role + dat_scaled + (1|groupID) + (1|groupID:ResponseId); the preregistered random-slope model did not converge. Robustness variant: 'Covariates' model adds item, fluency, and word count. In the human-AI arm the scored set includes GPT-4o's responses.

contrasts.reported: Base model: Condition (Human-Human) B = -0.065*** (SE 0.007), t = -9.69, p < .001; reference = AI-Human; N obs = 2,970, 139 groups. Role B 0.018 (0.004); Condition x Role B -0.021 (0.007), p = .005. Covariates model: Condition (Human-Human) B = 0.010 (0.008), t = 1.28, p = .201. Sign: coefficient is human-human minus human-AI.
contrasts.locator: p. 9, Table 2; p. 10, text; p. 11, Figure 2a-b

outcomes.name: AUT originality, human responses only (AI responses excluded)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Same CLAUS originality model ('Human-Only' column, with covariates item, fluency, word count) on human-generated responses only. Robustness: re-run with one randomly selected human per human-human pair to compare one person with one person.

contrasts.reported: Human-Only model: Condition (Human-Human) B = 0.029** (SE 0.010); text B = 0.0293, SE = 0.0104, t = 2.83, p = .005; N obs = 2,066, 137 groups. Random-one-human re-run: B = 0.027, SE = 0.011, t(175.5) = 2.518, p = .013. Positive coefficient = human-human higher.
contrasts.locator: p. 9-10, Table 2 Human-Only column; p. 10-11 text; p. 11, Figure 2c

outcomes.name: AUT forward flow (semantic distance between consecutive ideas in a pair's sequence)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Semantic distance = 1 - cosine similarity between consecutive responses within each pair, using paraphrase-multilingual-MiniLM-L12-v2 embeddings; linear regression of semantic distance on condition and idea sequence position. Full data truncated to first 20 ideas per pair ('pass' kept); human-only variant uses first 10 human ideas. The paper calls this a diversity measure (Hypothesis 2), but it compares ideas within one pair's sequence, not across pairs.

contrasts.reported: All responses: main effect of condition B = 0.091, SE = 0.094, t = 6.34, p < .001; idea sequence B = 0.003, SE = 0.001, t = 2.43, p = .015; human-human pairs show higher semantic distance. Human-only: condition B = 0.064, SE = 0.024, t = 2.65, p < .008; sequence p = .47; interaction p = .34. (SE 0.094 with t = 6.34 is as printed.)

outcomes.name: Spread of AUT originality scores (Levene's test on variance)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Levene's test (median-centered) comparing the variance of CLAUS originality scores between conditions; the paper labels it a diversity analysis (range of originality scores). Run on all responses and on human-only responses.

contrasts.reported: All responses: F(1, 3036) = 3.72, p = .054 (Fig. 3a shows wider spread for Human-AI). Human-only: F(1, 2132) = 0.15, p = .70.

outcomes.name: AUT elaboration (word count per response)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Word count per AUT response; mixed model word count ~ condition * role + dat_scaled + (1|groupID) + (1|groupID:ResponseId). Variants: Covariates model (item, fluency) and Human-Only model excluding AI responses. Word count is a computed length, not a category count; no better code exists in the list.

contrasts.reported: Condition (Human-Human): Base -7.08*** (0.55), t = -12.79; Covariates -9.13*** (0.63); Human-Only -5.04*** (0.64), N obs 2,066, 137 groups. Condition x Role B: Base -2.44*** (0.47); Human-Only -3.15*** (0.69). Reference = AI-Human. Descriptive: 3.34 words per idea (human-human) vs 12.7 (human-AI).
contrasts.locator: p. 13, Table 3; p. 13-14 text; p. 14, Figure 5; p. 9 descriptive text

outcomes.name: AUT fluency (responses per pair)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Average number of responses per pair, including the AI partner's responses in the human-AI arm. Descriptive only; used as a covariate elsewhere.

contrasts.reported: Human-human pairs: 10 responses on average (book 9.81, bottle 10.20); human-AI pairs: 11.7 (book 11.80, bottle 11.50). No SDs or test.
contrasts.locator: p. 9, Alternate Uses Task, Originality paragraph

outcomes.name: Short story originality (divergent semantic integration, DSI)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: DSI: semantic distance between all pairs of words in the story text (Johnson et al., 2022). Linear mixed model with condition, participant role, scaled DAT, random effect of group ID; variant adds word count. The paper does not state the reference category or the number of observations for this model.

contrasts.reported: Initial model: condition B = -0.006, SE = 0.008, t = -0.79, p = .431; role B = 0.003, SE = 0.007, p = .667; condition x role B = -0.019, SE = 0.010, p = .070. With word count: condition B = 0.006, SE = 0.008, t = 0.72, p = .472; condition x role B = -0.020, SE = 0.010, p = .045.
contrasts.locator: p. 14-15, Creative Short Story Task, Originality; p. 15, Figure 6

outcomes.name: Short story diversity contribution score across stories
outcomes.question: across_people
outcomes.measure_detail: Condition diversity = mean pairwise cosine dissimilarity (1 - cosine similarity) among all stories in a condition, using Sentence-BERT paraphrase-multilingual-MiniLM-L12-v2. Each story's diversity contribution = total diversity minus diversity computed without that story. Compared by Mann-Whitney U and two-sample Kolmogorov-Smirnov tests because distributions were non-normal.

contrasts.reported: Human-AI n = 72 pairs vs Human-Human n = 68 pairs: Mann-Whitney U = 2674, p = .347; Kolmogorov-Smirnov D = 0.217, p = .061. Shapiro-Wilk: Human-Human W = 0.856, p < .001; Human-AI W = 0.946, p = .004. No arm medians or means printed.
contrasts.locator: p. 7, Data Analysis; p. 15, Diversity; p. 15, Figure 7a

diversity_detail.metric: Leave-one-out diversity contribution score: condition mean pairwise cosine dissimilarity minus the same quantity with the story removed
diversity_detail.computed_over: All pairs of stories within a condition; each story's contribution relative to its condition's pool
diversity_detail.uncertainty: Mann-Whitney U test and two-sample Kolmogorov-Smirnov test on story-level contribution scores
diversity_detail.notes: One story per pair; in the human-AI arm each story is co-written by one person and GPT-4o, in the human-human arm by two people. Further details said to be in SI 2 (not in this PDF).

outcomes.name: Short story forward flow (semantic distance across sentence sequence), exploratory
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Exploratory forward flow: semantic distance between consecutive sentences regressed on condition, running sentence sequence, and their interaction. The text and Figure 7b describe human participants; whether AI sentences are excluded is not stated explicitly.

contrasts.reported: Condition main effect B = 0.002, SE = 0.016, t = 0.17, p = .90; running sequence B = 0.001, SE = 0.001, p = .14; condition x sequence B = 0.004, SE = 0.002, t = 2.37, p = .018; model R^2 = .014, F(3, 1762) = 8.60, p < .001. Human-human semantic distance rises across sentences; human-AI stays flat.

outcomes.name: Short story elaboration (word count)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Story word count; linear mixed model with condition, participant role, scaled DAT, random effect of group ID. Word count is a computed length; no better code exists in the list.

contrasts.reported: Intercept B = 133.36, SE = 5.34; condition B = -48.38, SE = 7.68, t = -6.30, p < .001 (human-human fewer words); role B = -12.04, SE = 5.59, p = .033; condition x role B = 7.14, SE = 8.05, p = .377.

outcomes.name: Individual Divergent Association Task (DAT) score, completed alone after the collaborative tasks
outcomes.question: after_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: DAT: participant names 10 unrelated words; score = mean pairwise semantic distance (GloVe, Common Crawl) x 100. Completed individually after the collaborative tasks, without the partner. The paper uses it as a baseline covariate, not as an outcome; it only reports arm averages.
outcomes.delay: same session, after the collaborative tasks

contrasts.reported: Humans in the paired (human-human) group: average DAT 75.4; humans in the AI group: 76.7. No SDs or test.
contrasts.locator: p. 4, Materials and Procedure (timing); p. 5, Verbal Creative Thinking Ability; p. 9, AUT Originality paragraph (means)

eligibility.reason: Participants were randomly assigned to a GPT-4o partner or a human partner (p. 4); 208 people (72 human-AI, 136 human-human; Table 1, p. 7). Outcomes are computed scores on the produced outputs (CLAUS originality, DSI, Sentence-BERT diversity, forward flow). Comparison type is ai_vs_active (AI partner vs human partner). Caveats: in the human-AI arm the scored outputs include GPT-4o's own contributions unless the 'human-only' models are used; the control arm has two people per output; AUT models report 139 of 140 groups.

one_line_finding: With a GPT-4o partner instead of a human partner, AUT originality of all pair responses was higher (Condition Human-Human B = -0.065, SE 0.007, Table 2, p. 9) but lower for human-only responses (B = 0.029, SE 0.010), and story diversity did not differ (Mann-Whitney U = 2674, p = .347, p. 15).
open_questions: AI here is a turn-taking co-creator rather than an assistant; role code 'other'. Does an AI-partner vs human-partner contrast fit ai_vs_active for the pooled with_ai estimate?
Which AUT originality record is primary: the preregistered all-responses model (includes AI's own ideas) or the human-only model (outcome of the person's own work)?

Levene's test on originality-score variance is labeled 'diversity' by the paper; coded here as construct 'other' under with_ai because it measures spread of a quality score, not similarity across people's outputs.
Forward flow measures distance between consecutive ideas within a pair; coded as flexibility (within-team variety), not diversity.
The individual DAT is completed after the collaborative tasks, so the arm means (75.4 vs 76.7) are formally an after_ai outcome, but the paper treats DAT as a baseline covariate and reports no test.
Whether n = 208 is before or after removing participants who admitted using outside internet or AI is not stated; AUT analyses use 139 groups.
notes: Role A/B (who starts) was also randomized within pairs and interacts with condition in several models; recorded in reported strings, not as separate contrasts. Table 2 and 3 notes list the reference item as 'Brick' although the items were bottle and book. Table 2 note's significance key is garbled ('p < .05. *p < .01. **p < .001'). The story models' condition coefficient lacks a stated reference category; AUT tables use AI-Human as reference. Self-reported partner perceptions (creativity, cooperativeness, ease, connection, IOS, AI attitudes) are not scored on output and are omitted. Codebook task type: AUT = divergent_test, story = creative_writing; the form's single task field uses divergent_test.
